correctness.rationale: A finite exchangeable retained-subset distribution is a mixture of uniform fixed-size subsets. For one concentration transfer (h,s)->(h+1,s-1), relabeling support indicators under exchangeability leaves two equal-weight opposite-parent configurations. Conditioning on other retained indicators and the number in the two specialist pools reduces the convex-payoff difference to Δφ(W+1+A)-Δφ(W+1+B), where A,B are hypergeometric counts in nested fixed sets with h>=s-1; A>=stB, so all convex differences are nonnegative. Integer majorization chains give the global convex order. Exact joint retention probabilities q_j give common mean a q1+b q2 and the sole variable covariance category is co-supported specialist pairs, yielding variance gap 2ΔT(q3-q4), positive exactly with positive retention mass at 3<=R<N. Independent exhaustive N=5,R=3 count gives balanced histogram (1,1,4,4) and concentrated (1,3,0,6) and variance gap 2/5; does not replace all-size proof.
